title: Rodrigo Niño (Naples) to Charles V, 19 March 1522, one ciphered paragraph (BNE MSS/20213/27; DECODE R1182)

documents.shelfmark: Biblioteca Nacional de España, MSS/20213/27; DECODE R1182

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf or on DECODE.

transcription.source: George Lasry CTTS project; BNE MSS/20213/27 f.1v, image I5904_P2 via DECODE R1182
transcription.notes: 8 cipher lines on one physical page; CTTS positions use 2070x1389 opening image. Two-folio letter, not three physical pages: DECODE has three attachments. 7 duplicated boxes removed; 3 null-group occurrences retained. Full cleartext letter not transcribed in this contribution.

system.summary: Homophonic graphic-sign substitution with an honorific code, two contextual word-part signs and syllable-shaped null groups.

diacritics.note: Ticks, strokes and nasal marks distinguish signs; they must not be split off as independent letters.

system.doubled_letters: Contextual special sign (50)=ll in ellos; one occurrence.
system.sibling_key: Lope Hurtado 1522 key (targets/lopehurtado/key_codes.tsv) compared by eye: different system
system.notes: 49 observed key classes, including one unresolved p/y class and contextual LL/ND. A 2017/2024 reconstruction of a related Niño cipher is known through Cryptiana; its alphabet was not used or compared directly.

prior_solution.where: Kolosova 2017 thesis (Cifra 15, pp. 452-459) and 2024 book, via Tomokiyo cryptiana spanish2C; key not seen here; not confirmed that this letter is one of her three; the September research called it the same system, but exact sign-key identity and exact-letter coverage remain unconfirmed.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry selected and transcribed the cipher with CTTS, recovered its initial key with CTTS built-in cryptanalysis, and directed refinement; attribution and prior-work timing supplied by the contributor.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and images P1-P2 of R1182 with the saved cookie.
Viewed the images: the letter is clear Spanish except one 8-line ciphered paragraph on f. 1v, opening [mer] and closing [mer por].
Tomokiyo spanish2C: Kolosova's Ko.15 (Rodrigo Niño 1522) is a simple substitution with nulls mer/mor/pu/por, which matches this block.
Fetched Kolosova's thesis from RODERIC (hdl 10550/66216): a 148-page version with no Niño chapter; the 2024 Salamanca book is paid.
Eye transcription of the 8 lines into ASCII sign codes (cipher_p2.txt), 128 words.

Simulated annealing with es-golden-age 5-grams, max two signs per letter; variants dropping '#' and/or 'o' as nulls and merging '#' into the preceding sign. Best -2.9 to -3.5 per char (Spanish about -1.1), unreadable.
George Lasry supplied CTTS transcription and positions; 260 elements in eight lines after duplicate-box and null-group corrections.
Lasry recovered the initial key with CTTS built-in cryptanalysis. User supplied this workflow attribution; no original solver seed/log is available in this contribution.
GPT 6.1 Sol and Anthropic Opus 5.5 refined the key and translation; source-based glyph splitting, contextual testing and edited Spanish text; one p/y class remains unresolved.

The earlier Cryptiana/Kolosova null-group description was consulted during PR preparation, after the initial CTTS alphabet recovery; mer and por were restored as nulls. No prior alphabet key or paragraph plaintext was applied.
decode.py reproduces all eight literal lines: 260 elements, 49 key entries, 3 null occurrences, 2 ambiguous occurrences, vowel maximum 4 and consonant maximum 3.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 258 tokens, 48 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -1.916 per letter; random keys -5.562 (z 6.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.836 (mean -2.862, z 35.1); annealer on the real text -2.494. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's CTTS transcription (ctts/transcription/1.txt) and edited reading (ctts/edited/1_edits.txt), the labelled transcription, literal, token-aligned and edited decryptions, the English translation and the CTTS key (key.txt) with its status table.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.916; polyphony 0.0; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.494

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry recovered the initial key with CTTS from the ciphertext; later contextual/source refinement and a literature-supported correction of mer/por nulls, without applying a published alphabet key or plaintext.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py, transcription.txt + key.json: 255 unambiguous assignments / 257 non-null cipher occurrences; two p/y occurrences counted unread. Assignment coverage, not an independent accuracy estimate.

texts.label: R1182, Rodrigo Niño (Naples) to Charles V, 19 March 1522: the eight-line cipher block (George Lasry, CTTS)
texts.summary: Rodrigo Niño, imperial ambassador at Naples, to Charles V, 19 March 1522. The ciphered paragraph begs the Emperor, for the love of God, to have Spain provide the pay of the rear-guard, since the soldiers have no bread to live on and the towns cannot bear the harm being done to them.
